fact_text: PSX publishes a periodically updated Shariah compliance list with screening ratios and explanatory notes, which investors can check company by company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A listed company fails the Shariah income screen when income from non-compliant sources, such as interest, exceeds 5% of its income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A company's investments in non-compliant places such as conventional banks should stay below 33%, a separate test from the income ratio.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dividends from a compliant stock are purified by donating the non-compliant share of income, and the analyst prefers applying that share to the gross dividend.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Capital gains on a stock that stays compliant need no purification, because gains are realised only on sale and the purification rule applies to dividends.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If a held stock turns non-compliant, the investor is given a window to sell it, and the eventual sale does not require purifying the capital gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Shariah status is re-determined from the latest annual financial statements on a periodic schedule, so a company can drift toward the ratio limit months before its status changes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Shariah-compliant ETFs can hold stocks with non-zero income ratios, so their dividends may still need purification, and the fund manager should be asked whether it purifies before distribution.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Some listed companies exceed the 5% income ratio yet remain classed as compliant, and the PSX document footnotes an explanation for each such exception.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Zakat, Dividends & Halal Stocks: All Your Shariah Compliance Questions Answered!' (YouTube transcript, undated)
